options: A program whose primary purpose is to read commands and run other programs
The physical case of a computer
questions.explain: The shell is the command-line interface between you and the operating system.
questions.evidence: A shell is a program whose primary purpose is to read commands and run other programs.

questions.q: What does a command-line interface (CLI) let users do?
options: Interact with a computer by reading and writing text
questions.explain: Text commands are easy to repeat, combine and automate.
questions.evidence: A command-line interface (CLI) allows users to interact with a computer by reading and writing text.

questions.q: What is your current working directory?
options: The one place you are in at any moment while using the shell
The folder where the shell program is installed
The root of the file system
questions.explain: Relative paths are interpreted from the current working directory (see pwd).
questions.evidence: at any time while we are using the shell, we are in exactly one place called our current working directory

questions.q: Why is it better to avoid spaces in the names of files and directories?
options: Spaces are not allowed by any operating system
Spaces are used to separate arguments on the command line
questions.explain: Use hyphens or underscores instead, e.g. north-pacific-gyre.
questions.evidence: since spaces are used to separate arguments on the command line it is better to avoid them in names of files and directories.

questions.q: A command is waiting for input and seems stuck. How do you get out?
questions.explain: Ctrl + C interrupts the running program.
questions.evidence: you can escape out of this state by holding down the control key ( Ctrl ) and pressing the letter C once

questions.q: What do loops let you do in the shell?
options: Repeat a command or set of commands for each item in a list
questions.explain: for filename in *.dat; do …; done applies the same steps to every file.
questions.evidence: Loops are a programming construct which allow us to repeat a command or set of commands for each item in a list.

options: A set of commands saved in a file — really a small program
A log of commands you typed yesterday
questions.explain: Saving repeated commands lets you re-run a whole workflow with a single command.
questions.evidence: a bunch of commands saved in a file is usually called a shell script

questions.q: Which command finds files and directories whose names match simple patterns?
questions.explain: grep searches inside files for lines that match; find searches for the files themselves.
questions.evidence: Use find to find files and directories whose names match simple patterns.

questions.q: When is UDP a suitable protocol?
options: When every packet must arrive in order
When speed and efficiency matter more than guaranteed delivery
questions.explain: Streaming, gaming and DNS lookups prefer speed; TCP guarantees delivery.
questions.evidence: UDP is suitable for applications where speed and efficiency are more important than guaranteed delivery

options: To reduce the number of IP addresses
To make the network easier to cable
To contain the impact of breaches and limit attackers' lateral movement
questions.explain: Isolated segments with strict access policies stop an intruder spreading.
questions.evidence: Network segmentation is used to improve security by containing the impact of potential breaches and limiting lateral movement for attackers within the network.

questions.q: What does the HTTPS guidance require for your service, including its APIs?
options: It must only be accessible through secure connections
It must allow plain HTTP for older browsers
It must use a separate domain for each page
It must block all mobile devices
questions.explain: Encryption in transit stops information being intercepted or modified.
questions.evidence: you must make sure your service (including APIs ) is only accessible through secure connections.
